title: uk-chilcot-inquiry: 892 numbered paragraphs render as <ol><li> with no id — only 60 of ~950 paragraphs citable
description:
The Chilcot Executive Summary's numbered paragraphs reach full.md as '13. To do so…', which Markdown reads as an ordered list: each renders as
  1. with no paragraph id. assets/generated/reports/uk-chilcot-inquiry/full-body.html has 60

    (vs 1,800–12,000 on comparable inquiries); almost the whole body, including every conclusion (e.g. para 20 'the diplomatic options had not at that stage been exhausted', para 432 legal basis 'far from satisfactory'), cannot be cited, quoted in an introduction, highlighted or linked. Found writing the introduction (reportsthatmatter-rcz.1), which it blocks. Fix direction: numberedFindings() already escapes '3437\. ' for Philip Morris, but only recognises lines indented past the margin; Chilcot's numbers sit at the margin, so adding numberedFindings() to uk-chilcot-inquiry/ingest.ts changes nothing (tried, full.md identical). Either make numberedParagraphs() (opt-in, used by Chilcot, Leveson, Hillsborough, Litvinenko, Saville) also write its paragraphs as 'N\. ' in blocksToMarkdown, or let numberedFindings accept margin-set numbers. Beware: the same '^N. ' lines exist in Litvinenko (111), Leveson (320), Hillsborough (384), Challenger (343) — gaining ids there may shift -2 dedupe suffixes on existing ids, so run the corpus check. Also: headings fused into the first numbered paragraph ('Introduction 1. In 2003…', 'Negotiation of resolution 1441 119. …') — see reportsthatmatter-ixe. No existing check caught this: a 'share of body text in

  2. without id' or 'paragraph ids per 1,000 words' check would.
close_reason:
Fixed and shipped. Root cause: numberedParagraphs() correctly split Chilcot's margin-set "N." lines into their own paragraph blocks, but blocksToMarkdown() only escaped a paragraph's leading number when block.finding was set (numberedFindings, indented findings like Philip Morris) — a margin-set numbering had no such tag, so every one of Chilcot's 892 numbered paragraphs reached Markdown as a bare "20. …", which Markdown reads as an ordered-list item with no id.

Fix: new opt-in pass escapeNumberedParagraphs() in @rtm/ingest (v0.14.1), declared alongside numberedParagraphs() only in uk-chilcot-inquiry/ingest.ts; pipeline() rejects it if declared without numberedParagraphs. Litvinenko, Leveson, Hillsborough and Challenger also have "^N. " lines but don't declare it — pnpm corpus check confirms only Chilcot moved (13/13 checked, 12 byte-identical).

Citable paragraphs: 64 -> 956 (all 892 numbered paragraphs now carry an id, e.g. #20-inquiry-s-view-diplomatic and #432-circumstances-which-ultimately-decided — text-derived, never positional, same convention as Philip Morris's findings).

Added a corpus-wide invariant check that would have caught this on day one: paragraph ids per 1,000 words (src/lib/density.ts, MIN_PARAGRAPH_IDS_PER_1000_WORDS = 4), wired into `pnpm corpus check` unconditionally. Fails on the pre-fix numbers (1.07/1000), passes on the fix (15.52/1000) and every other current report (floor 6.73/1000, jack-smith-vol1). Test: tests/density.test.ts. Noted on reportsthatmatter-b78.

Shipped: ingest PR #23 merged, v0.14.1 tagged on main; uk-chilcot-inquiry re-ingested and pushed; site PR #194 (fix) and #195 (changelog) merged; deployed to Cloudflare; published via publish-report; verify.sh green both locally and against https://reportsthatmatter.org. title: [bug] jack-smith-vol1 the-results-of-the-investigation: paragraphs split mid-sentence at page breaks, one continuation set as a block quotation (GH jack-smith-report#1)
description:
Reported by Rufus 2026-09-26: https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/jack-smith-report/issues/1 — page https://reportsthatmatter.org/reports/jack-smith-vol1/the-results-of-the-investigation.

Examples from the screenshots:
1. '...The throughline of all of Mr. Trump's criminal efforts was deceit-knowingly false claims of election' / new paragraph 'fraud-and the evidence shows that Mr. Trump used these lies...' — severed mid-phrase at printed p.3/4; continuation starts lowercase.
2. '...Mr. Trump also monitored legal developments' / new paragraph 'regarding the election and was on notice...' — severed mid-sentence, lowercase continuation.
3. '...could not have believed the specific fraud claims that they were' / block quotation 'making because the numbers they touted...Mr. Trump privately' / new paragraph 'acknowledged sounded "crazy"...' — one sentence broken into three blocks across p.5/6, the middle set as a quote (same skew/inset cause as kb4).

A paragraph ending without terminal punctuation followed by a paragraph/quote starting lowercase is almost always a page-break split. Fix in the pipeline (join across page break when previous ends mid-sentence and next starts lowercase or continues the sentence; treat a page-opening inset that continues a mid-sentence paragraph as continuation), never by hand in full.md. Measure corpus-wide before/after.
acceptance_criteria: All three examples read as continuous prose on the live page; corpus-wide count of (no terminal punctuation → lowercase-start paragraph/quote) pairs reported before and after; ingest check diffs understood; verify.sh passes.
notes:
2026-09-28 fix (unreleased). Two causes. (1) mergeAcrossPages looked past only ONE page marker. A paragraph filling a whole page leaves that page's marker behind it, so examples 1 and 2 (%%page 3#2%% %%page 4#2%%; %%page 5%% %%page 6%%) were never joined. (2) Skew-inset page openings arrive as quote blocks, which were never joined (example 3). Why no check caught it: severedSentenceCheck compares only the immediately next block (a page marker hides the split), counts quotes only, and is a 20% rate gate. Fix: opt-in pass pageBreakContinuations() plus a measure, pageBreakSplits(markdown), in ingest PR reportsthatmatter/ingest#15. Jack Smith declares it in jack-smith-report#2. Site PR #175 carries full.md, the corpus baseline (455→448) and editorial ids. Jack Smith pageBreakSplits: 8 → 0. Rendered page checked locally: all three examples each sit in one

. Integrator: tag ingest, bump the pin in the report repo and the site, re-ingest (full.md should not change), regenerate editorial.ts.

title: Footnote text leaking into body paragraphs (Jack Smith, Wall Street) — worst on landing-page links
description:
Footnote and citation text from the PDF lands inside body paragraphs instead of in sidenotes, so a reader following a link from a landing page meets a paragraph interrupted by source citations. For a separate session; Rufus, 2026-09-25.

Measured 2026-09-25 on the paragraphs the two landing pages link to (editorial/*.yaml, after pnpm prerender and pnpm editorial). Body text was extracted with extractParagraph, which drops sidenotes, then searched for citation markers (SCO-nnn, See ECF, Hearing Exhibit, GS MBS-E, Int. Tr., HSC Tr.):
- jack-smith-vol1: 5 of 21 affected. Fragment counts: most-part-co-conspirators-deceived-trump 21, december-14-the-date-eca-required 8, instance-trump-co-conspirator-1-called 4, remand-from-supreme-comi-s 1, trump-s-resort-intimidation-harassment 1.
- us-psi-financial-crisis: 1 of 17. traditionally-investments-holding-aaa-ratings has a Goldman citation block mid-sentence. Also between-2004-2007-moody-s (p.6) carries a Goldman put-option footnote.
- Jack Smith pp.26-28: photo captions merge with citations. p.32: OCR 'hostaoes b ''.

Where to fix: the pipeline (@rtm/ingest and each report's ingest.ts), not the output (AGENTS.md house rule). Likely the same footnote-block detection gap as ROADMAP's "Footnote-block leakage". See docs/report-preparation.md for the workflow.

Acceptance:
- Rerunning the measurement above shows 0 affected landing-page paragraphs for both reports.
- Paragraph ids cited in editorial/*.yaml still resolve (pnpm editorial passes) or are updated.
- ./scripts/verify.sh passes.

Blocks the launch (y2t.6) because launch traffic lands on these paragraphs.
notes:
2026-09-25 (overnight agent session). Fixed; awaiting orchestrator merge and publish of reportsthatmatter PR https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/reportsthatmatter/pull/158.

ROOT CAUSE, three parts:
(1) Measurement/site bug: extractParagraph stripped only <span class="sidenote">; a note over 400 chars renders as 'sidenote long', so its text stayed in the paragraph's plain text (also in share previews and cards). 3 of the 5 Jack Smith hits (21, 8 and 4 fragments) were correctly placed long sidenotes. Fixed in src/templates/report.ts with a test.
(2) Real Jack Smith leaks: pdftotext -layout puts note text ABOVE the page's first numbered note in two cases: a note running over a page break (its tail opens the next block with no number), and a note whose low-set superscript number drops to the line below its own first line ('40 See', a lone '104'). splitFootnoteBlock anchored on the first number, so that text stayed in the body: 10 citation 'paragraphs' plus 2 inline splices, splitting 5 sentences, including the landing paragraph most-part-co-conspirators-deceived-trump ('deliberately / [citations] / withheld from').
(3) PSI wrong sidenotes: contents-page page numbers after dot leaders and 'Long Beach, 75 out of 75' were linked as markers. withSidenotes resolves a number's definitions in order, so each bogus link gave later notes the wrong text (between-2004-2007-moody-s note 1 showed a Goldman put-option note).

FIX (pipeline, general passes): @rtm/ingest v0.12.17 (ingest PR #9) and v0.12.18 (PR #10), tags on the post-merge main commits. Run-over lines are carried as SplitPage.runOver and appended to the last note read. They are never parsed for numbers: one line starts '169 (Text messages...', which had derailed the note counter. This only applies on double-spaced pages; Litvinenko's single-spaced pages sit straight on their notes, and the unguarded rule moved paragraphs and a chapter heading (fixture test added). Displaced first lines are recognised by the short opening, the inset, and text continuing at the note margin. Also DOT_LEADER_BEFORE and COUNT_SOON_AFTER guards in linkInlineMarkers.

BLAST RADIUS (all reports regenerated fresh before/after, same poppler 26.08.0, every diff read): jack-smith-vol1 (intended), us-psi-financial-crisis (contents page and Long Beach only), challenger-accident and us-v-philip-morris (contents/hearing-list dot leaders and one '8 out of 11'). The other 7 are byte-identical. Paragraph ids: Jack Smith loses the 10 leaked ids, and 5 half-paragraph ids rejoin their paragraph. PSI contents entries' ids now carry their page number, so about 12 body headings drop a -2/-3 suffix. No body prose id moved otherwise. Editorial highlight withheld-from-elector-nommees-information repointed to most-part-co-conspirators-deceived-trump.

MEASUREMENT (issue's method): before, as filed: JS 5/21, PSI 1/17. Before, with extraction fixed: JS 2/21, PSI 0/17. After: JS 2/21, PSI 0/17. Whole Jack Smith report: 54/468 as filed, 23/468 with extraction fixed, 12/453 after. ASSUMPTION: the 2 remaining JS landing hits (remand-from-supreme-comi-s, trump-s-resort-intimidation-harassment) are the report's own in-body docket citations ('ECF No. 233.', 'See ECF No. 57 at 3 (...)'), checked against the PDF (PDF pp.144, 120). They are not leaks and must stay for fidelity, so the acceptance '0 affected' is treated as met: 0 leaked-footnote landing paragraphs in both reports. Of the 12 whole-report JS hits, 11 are that kind of in-body citation; 1 is a real leak (OCR-misnumbered note, filed as 4yp).

title: A numbered paragraph opener ("3.77 ") doesn't start a new paragraph when no blank line separates it from the one before
description:
Confirmed live in production: uk-litvinenko-inquiry/chapter-2-leaving-russia (https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/uk-litvinenko-inquiry/issues/2) shows paragraphs 3.77-3.81 -- five distinct numbered paragraphs -- all fused into one

, and 3.75+3.76 fused into another, on the same page where 3.82 onward render correctly, one per paragraph. Root cause, confirmed against the raw pdftotext -layout output: this report's own typesetting is inconsistent about whether a blank line separates consecutive numbered paragraphs. Where 3.82, 3.83, 3.84... have a real blank line between them, toBlocks correctly starts a fresh paragraph at each. Where 3.75-3.81 have NO blank line (each numbered opener sits flush against the previous paragraph's last line, both at indent 0 -- the "hanging indent" numbering style these reports use puts the number at the margin and the paragraph's own text one tab-stop in, matching ordinary continuation lines), nothing distinguishes the numbered opener from a continuation line, so it silently welds on. @rtm/ingest src/paragraphs.ts already has a function for exactly this number style -- opensNumberedParagraph(text), matching "7.1", "10.14", per its own comment "the paragraph numbering these reports run throughout" (plural — this convention isn't unique to Litvinenko) -- but it is used in exactly one place (the division-heading-continuation guard, line ~540) and never consulted by toBlocks' own startsParagraph decision, which is indent-only: const startsParagraph = !quoted[i] && indent > margin + 1; A numbered opener at indent 0 never clears margin+1, so it can never trigger a paragraph break on its own -- the function exists but the one place a paragraph actually gets split never asks it.
acceptance_criteria:
toBlocks treats a line matching opensNumberedParagraph as starting a new
paragraph regardless of indentation or a preceding blank line.
uk-litvinenko-inquiry's 3.75-3.81 render as five separate paragraphs.
pnpm ingest check + corpus check reviewed and accepted across every
report using this numbering convention (at minimum Litvinenko and
Leveson); no false-positive split introduced where a line coincidentally
opens with something matching the pattern (a decimal figure at a line
break, e.g. "3.5 million") -- checked by sampling the corpus diff, not
assumed safe from the regex alone.
notes:
Fixed via @rtm/ingest v0.12.7: a new opt-in pass, numberedParagraphs(),
declared on litvinenko-inquiry, uk-leveson-inquiry, and uk-hillsborough-
panel (the three reports confirmed to use this "N.NN" chapter.paragraph
numbering). toBlocks now reads a genuine two-part numbered opener as a
paragraph break regardless of indentation or a preceding blank line --
opensNumberedParagraph already existed for exactly this shape but was
consulted in only one place (a heading-continuation guard) and never by
toBlocks' own break decision.

Iterated through two real false-positive classes found by reading the
actual corpus diff, not by trusting the regex:
1. Applying it unconditionally moved every report, including ones that
   never use this convention -- Challenger's test-method appendices
   wrap decimal measurements onto their own line ("...compression of
   5.8 to" / "7.0 percent..."), and reading "7.0" as a paragraph opener
   severed a sentence mid-thought. Fixed by making it opt-in.
2. Even scoped to the three reports that do use the convention: a bare
   "N." (Litvinenko's "allocated room\n\n382. Mr Begak...", a room
   number) and a two-part number immediately followed by a quantity
   word ("suggested\n\n1.8 million people...", Leveson) both read as
   paragraph openers. Fixed by requiring both digit groups and adding
   a QUANTITY_WORD_FOLLOWS guard. 4 new tests cover the opt-in gate and
   both guards.

Verified against real data: litvinenko-inquiry +150 paragraphs,
uk-leveson-inquiry +1,818, uk-hillsborough-panel +90 -- all seven other
reports in the corpus completely unaffected (pnpm ingest check green
throughout). Word counts unchanged in all three (content re-segmented,
nothing lost). Sampled dozens of the ~2,058 new splits by hand across
all three reports, all correct, including the specific cases from
uk-litvinenko-inquiry#2 and both false-positive classes found along the
way. Corpus-baseline moves reviewed and accepted (paragraph permalinks
shifted, as they must when previously-merged paragraphs split). Full
local verify.sh green.

title: Make per-chapter footnote identities safe for Leveson
description: Leveson restarts footnote numbering by chapter, while the ingestion pipeline treats a number as report-global. Correct identity and rendering without making marker-linking unsafe.
acceptance_criteria: Every rendered Leveson footnote reference resolves to its own chapter-local definition; no output exceeds deployment asset limits; ingestion checks and rendered-page inspection confirm the result.
notes:
2026-09-11 — Fixed upstream in @rtm/ingest (v0.12.4), verified against real Leveson data, shipped corpus-wide.

Root cause: renderEndnotes/collectNotes/withSidenotes modelled a footnote's identity as its bare number, deduping/looking up by number alone. Any report where two genuinely different notes share a number -- Leveson's deliberate per-chapter restart, or (discovered along the way) OCR misreading a footnote marker's digits so it collides with an unrelated earlier note -- collapsed those notes into one merged definition, and every reference to that number resolved to whichever text won the collapse.

Fix: reference markers are untouched (no change to where/how a [^N] gets written). Definition RESOLUTION is now position-aware: renderEndnotes still merges adjacent same-number entries (exact repeats, page-break tails -- unchanged, same tests pass), but non-adjacent same-number entries stay separate definitions; collectNotes returns all of a number's definitions in document order; withSidenotes resolves each [^N] reference against them positionally (1st reference -> 1st definition, 2nd -> 2nd, ...). New unit + integration tests in @rtm/ingest (243 total passing). Tagged v0.12.4.

Real-data impact was much bigger than the bead described -- this wasn't Leveson-only. Re-ingesting under the fix moved 7 of 10 reports' footnote text (challenger-accident, columbia-accident, jack-smith-vol1, litvinenko-inquiry, uk-leveson-inquiry, us-deepwater-horizon, us-psi-financial-crisis), all verified by direct comparison: body text byte-for-byte identical in every case, only the Notes section changed, growing as merged blobs split back into correct definitions. us-deepwater-horizon was hit hardest -- 1,226 sidenotes, same count before and after, but the rendered page shrank 2.07MB -> 1.78MB because each sidenote now shows only its own text instead of a shared merged blob. All 10 reports pass pnpm ingest verify/check; pnpm corpus check diffs read and accepted (6 reports: footnote-only, zero citable-paragraph impact, confirmed by identical body byte-count; Leveson: real paragraph-id moves too, see below).

Leveson specifically: its own package.json was still pinned to v0.2.1 (never updated since migration), ~10 versions behind. Bumping it to get this fix meant adopting everything else the pipeline gained since too -- footnote recall in particular (8,605 footnotes now found vs the old ~1,680, most previously merged). This DOES move real Leveson paragraph-id citations (23 sections affected, mostly from a few headings losing a spurious 'CHAPTER' prefix that had been concatenating into the section title). Read and accepted deliberately -- see uk-leveson-inquiry's own commit (8fbc371) for the full account. Asset size checked explicitly given the bead's #103 history: full-body.html is 8.9MB, safely under the 25 MiB Cloudflare limit.

Verified via rendered-page inspection (the acceptance criteria's own requirement): of 62 Leveson footnote numbers with more than one resolved occurrence in the final HTML, all 62 now show correctly distinct text -- was effectively 0/63 correct on an earlier, not-yet-fully-baselined check.

Split off, not attempted here: reportsthatmatter-axw (linkInlineMarkers still links some non-footnote numbers -- a few dates, a repeated boilerplate block with a likely-dropped phone-number leading zero -- a pre-existing, separate defect that predates this fix and doesn't dominate the corpus the way the identity bug did, but is visible in spot checks).

Shipped: @rtm/ingest v0.12.4 (tagged, released); all 7 affected report repos on main/master; site repo pin bumped, all 10 reports aggregated, corpus-baseline.json accepted. ./scripts/verify.sh green throughout, multiple times, including after every baseline-accept round.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in @rtm/ingest v0.12.4, verified against real Leveson data (62/62 repeated footnote numbers now resolve to correct, distinct text), and shipped corpus-wide -- 7 of 10 reports had the same underlying bug (footnote definitions merging across unrelated notes when numbers collide), all re-ingested and verified. Residual, separate false-positive-linking issue split off to reportsthatmatter-axw.

title: us-lehman-examiner: sentences severed across page breaks (~25 paragraphs)
description:
Ingesting Volume 1 of the Valukas Report (reportsthatmatter-b7z) with @rtm/ingest v0.13.0 (contentsOutline() declared; also tried pageBreakContinuations(), no effect — see below): about 25 paragraphs are a single sentence in the source PDF that the page-break merge splits into two or three separate paragraphs, each getting its own paragraph id. Examples (full.md, current commit):

  "Lehman's failure to disclose the use of an accounting device to significantly and temporarily lower leverage, at the same time that it affirmatively represented those" / [paragraph break] / "\"low\" leverage numbers to investors as positive news, created a misleading portrayal of" / [paragraph break] / "Lehman's true financial health.80 Colorable claims exist against the senior officers..."

  One sentence, three paragraphs, three ids. The middle fragment happens to open on a quotation mark ("low"), which is a real quoted word *inside* the sentence, not a block quotation.

Tried `pageBreakContinuations()` (new in v0.13.0, "rejoins a sentence the page break left in pieces"): re-ingested with it declared and it made no measurable difference — the same ~25 fragments remain unjoined, most likely because its documented behaviour only rejoins a continuation that "opens in lower case" or is "a quotation opening a page after a paragraph that stops mid-sentence... when it opens in lower case, or when it stops mid-sentence too and runs straight into a lower-case paragraph," and explicitly leaves alone anything "opening on a quotation mark." Our fragments mostly continue on an ordinary capitalised word (a new clause of the same sentence, not a new sentence) or, in the case above, on a quotation mark that isn't introducing a block quotation at all — neither shape this pass targets.

Measured on the current committed full.md: of 1,539 paragraph-like blocks, roughly 25 genuine cases end without terminal punctuation and are continued as the next paragraph (a rough heuristic list of the false positives to exclude — headings, table fragments, dashed rules — is in this session's working notes; happy to hand over the exact script).

No existing fidelity check catches this: severedSentenceCheck watches for a paragraph running straight into a *quotation* block, not for a plain paragraph-to-paragraph split with no quotation involved.
acceptance_criteria: A shared pass (or an extension to pageBreakContinuations) rejoins sentences split across a page break into ordinary continuing paragraphs — including the case where the continuation opens on a quotation mark that is part of the original sentence, not a new block quotation — without turning genuine quotations into merged prose elsewhere in the corpus. A fidelity check flags a paragraph that plausibly ends mid-sentence (no terminal punctuation) so this doesn't ship silently again.

title: ingest: listedDivisions() promotes a contents page's own listing lines as duplicate headings when isContentsPage doesn't recognise it

title: us-duelfer-report: rotated chapter-tab side banner splices into body text (FIXED, pending ingest v0.14.0 release)
description:
Volume I of the Duelfer Report (Comprehensive Report of the Special Advisor
to the DCI on Iraq's WMD) sets each chapter's name as a rotated, black
side-banner graphic running the full height of every page ("Regime Strategic
Intent" / "Regime Finance and Procurement"). pdftotext's reading order drops
this banner's text into the line stream at an essentially arbitrary point on
the page -- not consistently at a page edge -- so `runningFurniture()` (which
only strips repeated lines at a page's top/bottom edge) does not catch most
occurrences. `columns()` is also declared (the report is genuinely
two-column in many sections) but does not help with this third, non-column
sidebar zone.

Measured on the current ingest (columns() + runningFurniture() +
listedHeadings(), @rtm/ingest v0.12.21): of 2511 paragraphs, the banner
fragment "Regime Strategic" appears mid-text (not as part of the legitimate
phrase "Regime Strategic Intent") 50 times, and "Regime Finance" (not part of
"Regime Finance and Procurement") 92 times -- 142 total splices across 451
pages, roughly one every three pages. Examples (full.md, current run):

- "was at the point of collapse. His rationale for this Regime Strategic by
  building many palaces the US would be unable to ascertain his whereabouts
  and thus target him." -- the banner is spliced mid-sentence, and the clause
  joining "for this" to "by building" reads as if words are missing around
  the splice.
- "Huwaysh was sacked as Minister of Industry in Regime Strategic ostracized
  for nine years."
- TOC lines are corrupted the same way: "Contents Regime Strategic Key
  Findings -- 1", "Annexes Regime Strategic A. The Quartet...".

Because the chapter contents pages are corrupted by the same defect,
`listedHeadings()` (added to suppress a *different*, worse defect -- see
below) cross-checks candidate headings against a corrupted contents list and
ends up rejecting nearly every real heading too: the volume renders with a
single heading ("Notes") and prerenders to only 2 sections for a 453-page,
168,000-word document.

Without `listedHeadings()`, heading detection instead produces 12 headings,
none of them real chapter/section titles -- e.g. "## Annex C: Regime
Strategic" (truncated by the same banner splice), "## TOTAL" and "## Crude
Oil" (table cells), "### Engineer Azmy Khrisat 1. Mr. Saddam Zaban Hasan"
(a list of names on their own lines), "### O. Box" (a mangled "P.O. Box").

Separately, the report also has a false block quote: the "Acknowledgements"
byline "Acknowledgements (12 September 2004 2330)" renders as a blockquote
(indented, quote-styled) on the report's own first page -- it is not a
quotation. And a stray pilcrow character ("¶") renders as its own bullet
list item at least once (seen just above "Saddam went on a palace and mosque
building extravaganza..."), a fragment of a paragraph-mark glyph in the
source that should have been dropped.

This needs a pass that can identify and strip a non-edge, non-column
furniture zone (the rotated side banner) before line ordering -- geometry-
aware, since the banner sits in a fixed horizontal band down one side of
every page, distinct from both text columns. Per the site's report-
preparation.md instructions, no pass was written for this while ingesting
the report; this bead records the defect with examples and counts for
whoever picks it up (shared pass if the pattern recurs elsewhere in the
corpus, otherwise a pass the report declares in its own ingest.ts).

title: us-lehman-examiner: footnote markers not linked in ~15% of body references
description:
Ingesting Volume 1 of the Valukas Report (Lehman Brothers examiner, reportsthatmatter-b7z) with @rtm/ingest v0.12.21 (default passes, no report-declared passes needed otherwise): footnote *definitions* are all correctly extracted (687 defs, `pnpm ingest verify`'s "every footnote reference has a note" check is green), but a large minority of *inline markers* are never linked into `[^N]` form — they stay as bare digits fused to the preceding word or number, exactly like the source PDF's superscript, e.g.:

  - "reported record revenues of nearly $60 billion and record earnings in excess of $4 billion for its fiscal year ending November 30, 2007.2 During January 2008..." (marker 2, unlinked; compare marker 56 two paragraphs later, which IS linked: `...to a cause of action available to the estate."[^56]`)
  - "Lehman used Repo 105 for no articulated business purpose except \"to reduce balance sheet at the quarter‐end.\"24 Rather than sell assets..." (marker 24, unlinked)
  - Worse, inside a financial table rendered as run-on prose: "Reported Net Leverage Leverage Without Repo 105 Q4 2007 $38.6 B71 16.172 17.873" — markers 71/72/73 are fused directly onto the numeric values ($38.6 B + marker 71; 16.1 + marker 72; 17.8 + marker 73), making the printed figure and the footnote number visually indistinguishable in the rendered page.

Measured on the committed full.md (before any report-declared pass): of ~817 total marker occurrences, 122 (108 distinct note numbers, ~15%) are unlinked bare digits; 695 are correctly linked `[^N]`. Not confined to the start of the document — unlinked markers recur throughout (spot-checked up to marker 689 near the end).

No existing fidelity check catches this: "every footnote reference has a note" only checks that a `[^N]` reference has a matching `[^N]:` definition; it says nothing about markers that were never converted to `[^N]` form in the first place, so this whole class of defect is invisible to `pnpm ingest verify`.

This looks like a shared-library gap (footnote inline-marker linking, `linkInlineMarkers`/`linkFlushMarkers` in @rtm/ingest), not something this report's own `ingest.ts` can fix by composing existing passes — flagging for the pipeline rather than writing a new pass myself, per this session's instructions. Needs someone who can reproduce against `us-lehman-examiner`'s archive PDF (pinned sha256 in its ingest.ts) to find why only a subset of markers link.
acceptance_criteria: A shared-pipeline fix (or a named cause ruled report-specific) makes us-lehman-examiner's re-ingested full.md link all 817 footnote marker occurrences to their [^N] definitions, or explains why some are correctly left bare. A new fidelity check (or an extension to the existing footnote check) catches an unlinked-but-defined marker so this class doesn't ship silently again.

title: pnpm cards: render one card per editorial card:true highlight
description: scripts/cards.mjs only renders a curated card per docs/share-quotes.yaml entry (keyed report/paragraph), plus one plain default per report. It doesn't render a card per editorial/<id>.yaml highlight with card: true, of which there are 61 across the 11 reports. Because of this, pnpm posts (reportsthatmatter-y2t.3) deliberately puts every editorial-origin queue item on the report's plain default card rather than a curated one — even where a share-quotes card happens to exist for that paragraph, since it may show different words. Fix: extend cards.mjs to render a card per (report, paragraph, quote) for every approved editorial highlight with card: true, and update src/lib/posts.ts's resolveCandidate to prefer that specific card for editorial-origin candidates. Natural companion: fold docs/share-quotes.yaml into the editorial files (plan's track A6), which would let cards.mjs read one source instead of two.

title: linkInlineMarkers links a number across a block boundary, fusing the next paragraph into the previous block
description: In @rtm/ingest footnotes.ts linkInlineMarkers matches /([.,;:!?"')])\s+(\d{1,4})(?=\s|$)/ — \s+ spans the blank line between markdown blocks, so a block ending in punctuation followed by a block opening with a known note number is fused: 'VIII. DEFENDANTS HAVE VIOLATED 18 U.S.C. §1962(d)' + '18 U.S.C. § 1962(d) provides...' became one heading with [^18] (us-v-philip-morris). Changing \s+ to [ \t]+ moves 5 other reports: us-deepwater-horizon +209 paragraphs, litvinenko +53, uk-leveson +10, us-psi +8, jack-smith-vol1 +5 (paragraph counts rise because blocks stop fusing) — needs diff review per report before landing.

title: Chilcot Executive Summary: most section headings are set in plain title case and are not recovered as structure
description:
The Executive Summary's own front contents (PDF p.5-6, printed pages 1-2) lists 88 section/subsection entries. With `listedHeadings()` declared (uk-chilcot-inquiry/ingest.ts), only 13 come out as `##`/`###` headings in full.md -- the 13 that happen to be set ALL CAPS in the body ("LOOTING IN BASRA", "TRANSITION", etc, all in the post-conflict chapter). The other 75, including top-level sections ("Introduction", "Why Iraq? Why now?", "Weapons of mass destruction", "Key findings"), are set in plain sentence/title case with no numbering, no lettering and no division label ("Part"/"Chapter"/"Section N"), so `isHeadingLine()` never treats the line as heading-shaped in the first place -- `listedHeadings()` only gates candidates isHeadingLine already proposes, it cannot promote a line isHeadingLine rejects. The result: a body line such as "UK policy before 9/11" runs straight into the numbered paragraph after it with no break at all ("UK policy before 9/11 26. Before the attacks on the US..."), and the report reads as one long undifferentiated stream of numbered paragraphs for most of its length.

Examples (all confirmed against `pdftotext -layout`, which shows the heading on its own line with a blank line before it and no distinguishing typography the text layer preserves):
- "Introduction" (page 4) -- fused into the paragraph below.
- "The UK decision to support US military action" (page 6) -- fused: "The UK decision to support US military action 24. President Bush decided...".
- "UK policy before 9/11" (page 6) -- fused: "UK policy before 9/11 26. Before the attacks on the US...".
- "Why Iraq? Why now?" (page 40), "Weapons of mass destruction" (page 69), "Key findings" (page 111) -- all fused the same way.
- 75/88 contents entries in total are missing as headings; run `grep -c "^#" reports/uk-chilcot-inquiry/full.md` (14, including the endnotes "## Notes") against the 88-entry contents list to reproduce the count.

This would need a shared-pipeline change (a pass that, given `listedHeadings`, treats a body line as heading-shaped when it exactly equals a contents entry -- letter for letter -- even without caps or numbering) or a report-owned pass along the lines of Challenger's `isolateDivisionLabels`. Per this session's instructions, no such pass was written; the Executive Summary ships to stage 1 with this limitation recorded in PROCESSING.md.

A second, smaller defect on the same contents page: one entry ("The predicted increase in the threat to the UK as a result of military action in Iraq", ending in the page-number leader "47") had its own leader digit "47" mistaken for an inline footnote marker and rendered as `[^47]`, fusing it with the next entry ("The UK's relationship with the US") into one list item. Source (`pdftotext -f 5 -l 5 -layout`) shows these as two entries on separate lines with a blank line between them; nothing in the source suggests a footnote there.
notes: Fixed, not yet shipped (per coordinator request mid-session, overriding the original file-a-bead instruction). New opt-in pass unmarkedHeadings() in @rtm/ingest: reportsthatmatter/ingest#19 (branch fix/chilcot-headings, commit 2d823b5) -- a line with no heading shape of its own still opens a heading when it matches a contents entry letter for letter and the preceding line on the same page ends cleanly (guards against a heading opening on a sentence continued from the page before -- found one real case, 'reconstruction.' on p.85, which coincides with a genuine heading elsewhere). Report repo: reportsthatmatter/uk-chilcot-inquiry#1, pinned to the ingest commit pending the real v0.13.0 tag. Recovers 69/88 contents-listed headings (up from 13/88), zero false positives verified against the whole document. Checked directly against the corpus: us-v-philip-morris (contentsOutline) and challenger-accident (listedHeadings) both byte-identical when rebuilt against this ingest commit -- no other report moves. Remaining 19/88: page-opening headings (no prior line on that page to check), two-line-wrapped titles, and the one contents-entry-fused-with-footnote-marker case -- all recorded in PROCESSING.md. Not merged/tagged/deployed -- needs: ingest PR merged + tagged v0.13.0, report repo repinned to the tag, site's own ingest pin bumped, re-ingest + re-verify (site PR #181).
close_reason: Shipped in release 2 (ingest v0.14.0): unmarkedHeadings() pass recovers 69 of 88 contents-listed headings with no shape of their own. Merged via reportsthatmatter/ingest#19, reportsthatmatter/uk-chilcot-inquiry#1 and reportsthatmatter/reportsthatmatter#181.

description: pageBreakContinuations (ingest#15) is opt-in; only jack-smith-vol1 declares it. pageBreakSplits count (paragraph+quote+skewQuote) per report, 2026-09-28: uk-leveson-inquiry 36 (35 quote, 1 skew), us-v-philip-morris 16 (quote), challenger-accident 9 (5 quote, 4 skew; 7 are OCR noise), us-911-commission 5 (3 quote, 2 skew, the skews are endnote lists), columbia-accident 4, uk-hillsborough-panel 4, uk-saville-inquiry 2, litvinenko/psi/deepwater 0, jack-smith 8→0. Hillsborough, Columbia and Saville cases looked like genuine continuations on a skim.

title: [epic] Systematic test harness for report processing: catch rendering/structure defects before readers do
description:
Rufus, 2026-09-27, on reportsthatmatter-ca3 (GH jack-smith-report#1): why aren't these being caught? Readers keep finding defects the pipeline should detect itself: paragraphs severed at page breaks, body text set as block quotations, footnote text in the body, headings made from body text, lost paragraph ids, truncated headings. Each is fixed one by one as a bug bead, with nothing that would catch the class next time.

Goal: a systematic harness that measures text/structure quality across the whole corpus on every ingest change, so regressions and unfixed classes are visible without a human reading pages.

Not for this session. Plan it properly. First step (child bead): build a catalogue of examples of what we have been missing, so we know the shape of the problem. Then search for systematic solutions (e.g. corpus-wide invariant checks / lint rules with counts per report, golden-page fixtures against the PDF, differential checks between pdftotext and other extractors, sampled LLM or human review, a 'defect budget' per report in verify).
acceptance_criteria: A written plan (docs/design/...) agreed with Rufus, derived from the examples catalogue, with child beads for implementation.

comments.author: Rufus Pollock
comments.text:
Added one corpus-wide invariant check as part of fixing reportsthatmatter-4qw (Chilcot's 892 numbered paragraphs rendering as an ordered list with no id): paragraph-ids-per-1,000-words, in src/lib/density.ts (paragraphDensityCheck), wired into `pnpm corpus check` (scripts/corpus.mjs) so it runs unconditionally on every report, not just on a baseline diff — the Chilcot defect shipped for a full release without moving any baseline, since a baseline records whatever shipped, not whether it was right.

Threshold MIN_PARAGRAPH_IDS_PER_1000_WORDS = 4, calibrated the same way ingest's digitDensityCheck is: measured across the 13-report corpus (2026-09-28), the legitimate floor is jack-smith-vol1 at 6.73/1000; pre-fix Chilcot measured 1.07/1000; post-fix Chilcot measures 15.52/1000. Threshold sits well below the legitimate floor and well above the broken value. Test: tests/density.test.ts — fails on the pre-fix numbers, passes on the fix and on every other current report.

This is exactly the kind of "corpus-wide invariant check with counts per report" this epic is scoping — a small, narrow instance of it. Worth folding into whatever systematic harness comes out of b78.1's catalogue rather than treated as separate.

title: Catalogue the defects readers and agents have found that the pipeline missed
description: First step of reportsthatmatter-b78. Go through closed and open bug beads (labels ingestion, report ids), GitHub issues on the report repos, and handoff notes; record each missed defect as an example: report, URL/paragraph id, defect class (page-break split, false block quote, footnote-in-body, heading from body text, missing id, truncated heading, ...), how it was found (reader, agent writing an intro, verify), and whether any existing check could have caught it. Output: docs/design/<date>-quality-harness/examples.md with a tally by class. Do not design the solution here.
acceptance_criteria: examples.md exists with at least every defect class from the existing bug beads, each with 1+ concrete example and a count; tally by class and by how-found.
notes:
missing id: non-ASCII paragraph ids (U+02BC etc.) absent from meta.paragraphToSection because ingest's paragraphIndex()/extractPassages() read ids back out of HTML with /[a-z0-9-]+/ while paragraphId() itself allows any \p{L}\p{N} — columbia-accident 176, uk-leveson-inquiry 4, us-911-commission 2, us-v-philip-morris 2, jack-smith-vol1 1 (reportsthatmatter-4k6). Found by an agent writing the Columbia introduction noticing it had to avoid paragraphs; no check (verify.sh, ingest check, corpus check) caught it, because corpus check fingerprints exactly the ids these same functions produce — a shared blind spot in the producer and the checker.
- page-break split hidden behind 2+ page markers / continuation set as a block quote at a skewed page top: jack-smith-vol1 the-results-of-the-investigation ('claims of election'/'fraud-and…'). Found by a reader (Rufus, GH jack-smith-report#1). Not caught: severedSentenceCheck looks only at the next block, and only at quotes. New measure pageBreakSplits (ingest#15) catches it (corpus: 84 splits before).
deepwater (2026-09-28): book gutter — even pages 4-5 cols further in turned 816 paragraphs into blockquotes, no check caught it (a 'quote share by page parity' or 'quote share of body' check would); chapter openers with title lines and no blank folded into first paragraph (no check on headings vs contents); page-foot photo credit swallowing the cross-page continuation.
Chilcot Executive Summary (reportsthatmatter-rcz, defect bead reportsthatmatter-ixe): defect class "heading fused into body text" (inverse of the usual "body text mistaken for heading"). 75 of 88 contents-listed section/subsection headings are plain title case with no caps/numbering/division-label signal, so isHeadingLine() never proposes them as heading candidates and listedHeadings() has nothing to gate -- they run straight into the paragraph after them, e.g. "UK policy before 9/11 26. Before the attacks on the US on 11 September 2001 (9/11), the UK was pursuing...". Found by: agent doing the stage-1 ingest, reading full.md against the source contents page. No existing check catches it -- `pnpm ingest verify`'s only heading check is "document has headings" (count > 0), which 14 recovered headings satisfies. Second smaller example, same report: a contents entry's own page-number leader digit ("47") was mistaken for an inline footnote marker and rendered as `[^47]`, fusing two separate contents entries into one list item -- defect class "spurious footnote marker from unrelated digit".
- (9ek, us-v-philip-morris) Paragraphs opening 'N. ' render as <ol><li> with no id: 4,088 findings were uncitable and every gate passed. A check could count top-level <ol> not inside a blockquote.
- (9ek) Running-furniture detection masks digits, so record citations recurring at page edges ('1350 at 1346 (US 63531).') were deleted: ~270 lines lost, not caught because retention is 96.7% anyway.
- (9ek) Per-page double-spacing detection missed 268 quote-heavy pages -> one paragraph per line. A check could flag runs of short paragraphs that do not end in sentence punctuation.
- (72f/yun) linkInlineMarkers spans blank lines, fusing a paragraph into the heading above as a 'note'. A check could flag headings containing [^N] followed by more than a few words.
tk8 (Columbia): (1) running-furniture stripped repeated-with-digits lines that were not furniture ('CHAPTER 1'…'CHAPTER 11', 'ENDNOTES FOR CHAPTER n'), dropping every chapter heading and taking the chapter number as the printed page — no check flags a printed page sequence that jumps backwards (…19, 1, 22… / …47, 3, 50…). (2) Also lost real text: citation tails like '11, 2001.' stripped as footers in 9/11/Philip Morris/Hillsborough — word-retention % didn't notice. (3) Speaker labels moved across a column split and first letters eaten ('light:', 'MACS:') — words-not-in-source missed it because 'light' is a word. (4) Sidebar/figure caps lines as h2 sections (107 in Columbia), so body text filed under the wrong section — no check compares headings to the report's own contents list. (5) Missing numbered sections the contents lists (1.3, 6.3…) — same gap. (6) Literal '#' paragraph rendered as h1.
us-lehman-examiner (Valukas Report Vol 1, reportsthatmatter-b7z): two defect classes found ingesting with @rtm/ingest v0.12.21, neither caught by pnpm ingest verify — filed as reportsthatmatter-0bf (footnote markers) and noted here (master table of contents), examples below.

1. footnote-in-body / unlinked markers (reportsthatmatter-0bf): 122/817 (~15%) inline footnote markers stay bare digits (e.g. "...ending November 30, 2007.2 During January 2008") instead of linking to [^N], including markers fused into numeric table values ("$38.6 B71 16.172" — marker glued onto the printed figure itself). Found by: agent reading rendered output during report-preparation (report-preparation.md step 3's "read the output, not just the counts"). No check could have caught it: "every footnote reference has a note" only checks [^N] vs [^N]: pairing, not whether a marker was ever converted to [^N] form.

2. front-matter table of contents rendered as body content: Volume 1's PDF opens with the whole 9-volume/2,200-page report's master contents (~1,900 of ~4,000 full.md lines) before Volume 1's own text begins. Entries are dot-leader label+page fused with no space ("Barclays....................703"); the render step splits them into readable bullets ("- (f) Barclays — 703"), which is good for a reader, but the source-word tokenizer that losslessCheck uses never adds the split-off trailing-digit token to its source vocabulary (it only does this for footnote-marker stems), so a document with a long enough dot-leader contents section can fail losslessCheck's <0.1%-foreign-words threshold purely from this (us-lehman-examiner: 152/67598 ≈0.22%) even though nothing was actually invented. Separately, some contents entries lose their own numbers ("## VOLUME" heading with no volume number) and a roman-numeral page marker ("xi") leaks into the bullet list as its own line. Likely addressed by the in-flight contentsOutline pass (ingest PR #18, targeted v0.13.0) rather than needing a new bead — watching for that tag before deciding whether to file one.
us-duelfer-report (Duelfer Report Vol I, stage-1 ingest, 2026-09-28): a new
defect class not yet in the tally -- a rotated, full-page-height side-banner
graphic (the chapter-name tab) whose text is inserted mid-line at an
arbitrary point in the reading order, not at a page edge, so the existing
`runningFurniture()` (edge-only) pass cannot catch it. 142 splices counted
across 451 pages (grep for the two chapter-name fragments minus their
legitimate in-prose uses). Example: "was at the point of collapse. His
rationale for this Regime Strategic by building many palaces the US would be
unable to ascertain his whereabouts..." Found by: agent doing the ingest,
reading full.md and the rendered page (verify.sh's word-count and
severed-quotation checks both passed). Also collapsed heading detection to 1
heading for a 453-page report once `listedHeadings()` was added to suppress
a worse defect (garbage headings from table cells/name lists), because the
contents pages are corrupted by the same banner splice and no longer

title: challenger-accident: Conclusions' key sentence severed across p. 4-5 (block quotation + orphan paragraphs)
description: In the Conclusions (printed pp. 4-5), the indented passage after 'In other areas, the Committee reached somewhat different conclusions than the Rogers Commission:' renders as a block quotation that stops mid-sentence ('...poor technical decision-making over a period of several years by top NASA'), and the rest continues as separate id'd paragraphs 'and contractor personnel, who failed to act decisively to solve the increasingly serious anomalies in the Solid' and 'Rocket Booster joints.' (ids contractor-personnel-who-failed-act, rocket-booster-joints). Same pattern at 'there-no-sense-urgency-their' ('...Rather,') / 'nasa-chose-continue-fly-flawed'. A stray "conclusion.'" footnote mark sits in the quote. This is the report's central departure from the Rogers Commission and cannot be quoted cleanly; the introduction (g0w.7.6) paraphrases it instead. Also: the compilation's '(9) only by the manufacturer...' paragraph (9-only-manufacturer-which-can) is the severed end of Issue 2 finding 2.
notes:
This is the ca3 page-break-continuation class for at least 2 of its 3 instances: 'over a period of several years by top NASA' (page 4) / 'and contractor personnel, who failed...' (page 5) is a textbook page-break split (no terminal punctuation, lower-case continuation, exactly one %%page%% marker between); the compilation's '(9) only by the manufacturer...' is the same shape. Adopted @rtm/ingest's pageBreakContinuations() (reportsthatmatter-ca3, merged in v0.13.0) in ingest.ts. Result: fixes the Issue 2/Finding 2 instance of the '...recipes known / only by the manufacturer...' sentence (now one paragraph) but NOT the Conclusions block quotation -- that one doesn't resume as a quotation on the far side of the page break (it resumes as plain paragraphs), which is outside the shape pageBreakContinuations currently merges (paragraph-into-quotation, not quotation-into-paragraph), so it's still 3 separate blocks. Also NOT a page-break case: 'There was no sense of urgency...Rather,' / 'NASA chose to continue to fly...' splits mid-page (no %%page%% marker between them at all) -- a different, still-unexplained mid-paragraph blank-line artifact inside the same block quote, left as-is. Net: Challenger should keep pageBreakContinuations() (real improvement, already declared), but the Conclusions' central departure from the Rogers Commission remains unquotable cleanly -- the introduction (g0w.7.6) is right to paraphrase it rather than wait for this. Filing a narrower gap in pageBreakContinuations (quotation resuming as prose after a mid-sentence page break) is a decision for whoever owns reportsthatmatter-ca3/kb4, not done here.
Release 2 (ingest v0.14.0, PR challenger-accident#1): partially fixed. pageBreakContinuations was adopted for this report (also referenced by that PR) and rejoins many page-break-split paragraphs elsewhere, but the specific defect described here is unchanged after re-ingest: the Conclusions block quotation still stops mid-sentence at '...top NASA' (full.md line ~175) with the orphaned continuation still separate ('and contractor personnel...Solid' / 'Rocket Booster joints.', full.md lines 179/181), and the compilation's '(9) only by the manufacturer...' stray paragraph is also still separate (full.md line 259). description:

notes:
Fixed in @rtm/ingest: paragraphIndex() (sections.ts) and extractPassages()'s CITABLE_UNIT (passages.ts) read ids back out of rendered HTML with /[a-z0-9-]+/, but paragraphId() (markdown.ts) already allowed any \p{L}\p{N} character — so a non-ASCII opening word produced an id neither lookup could see. Widened both regexes to a shared PARAGRAPH_ID_CHARS = [\p{L}\p{N}-]+ (u flag) exported from markdown.ts, so id-consumers can't drift from the id-producer again. Did not touch slugify() or paragraphId() — no paragraph id changes shape. Ingest PR (not merged): https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/ingest/pull/14 Branch: fix/non-ascii-paragraph-ids Added failing-first tests (tests/markdown.test.ts, tests/passages.test.ts) reproducing the Columbia example; confirmed both fail against the pre-fix pattern and pass with the fix. pnpm test: 388/388. pnpm typecheck, pnpm check-dist both clean. Non-ASCII

title: uk-leveson-inquiry: chapter headings attached to the wrong body text
description:
In uk-leveson-inquiry's rendered meta.json/sections, several chapter headings are attached to the wrong paragraph, so the section they head is not what the heading says.

Clearest case: the heading "Chapter 7: Conclusions and recommendations for future regulation" (the real Part K chapter, in which Leveson sets out and defends his recommended regulatory model) is attached at two places that are NOT that chapter — the very start of Part A (slug chapter-7-conclusions-and-recommendations-for-future-regulation, page ~3, which actually opens Part A's real content) and its own front-matter TOC line. Meanwhile the chapter's real content — numbered paragraphs 7.1-7.12, e.g. "This legislative proposal does no more than ensure an appropriate degree of independence... This is not, and cannot be characterised as, regulation of the press" — sits ungrouped under the unrelated heading '"GUARANTEE OF MEDIA FREEDOM' (slug guarantee-of-media-freedom-2, p.1781), which is itself a different chapter's (mislabeled?) heading.

Second case: "PART H" (slug part-h, p.999) is followed by no further heading until p.1122, so it silently swallows several real chapters — Part H's own Chapters 1-7 (Introduction through Summary of recommendations, pp.999-1111) AND the start of Part I (press and politicians) — into one ~120-page section.

Likely cause: the heading-detection pass matches on heading TEXT appearing in large font (both the real chapter opening and, separately, that same text rendered large in a volume's front-matter TOC), but doesn't reliably anchor to the correct occurrence's body position — similar in kind to the truncated-heading class of bug already tracked (reportsthatmatter-b5x), but here the heading is complete and simply mis-positioned rather than cut off.

Impact: paragraph ids and citations are unaffected and resolve correctly (verified via pnpm paragraphs/pnpm editorial) — only the section/contents-page grouping and headings are wrong. Worked around in editorial/uk-leveson-inquiry.yaml's reading guide with title overrides on the two affected reading-guide entries (guarantee-of-media-freedom-2 -> "Chapter 7: Conclusions and recommendations for future regulation"; chapter-the-press-and-the-police-conclusions-and-recommendations and part-l-summary-of-recommendations also overridden for their shouted all-caps headings, a separate, minor issue). The contents page itself still shows the misattached headings uncorrected, since title overrides only apply within the editorial reading guide.

Fix belongs in the ingest pipeline (@rtm/ingest heading-detection pass), not the editorial file, per AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: uk-leveson-inquiry re-ingested with @rtm/ingest heading-detection fix; chapter-7-conclusions-and-recommendations-for-future-regulation's section boundary covers paragraphs 7.1-7.12 (the actual Chapter 7 content) rather than Part A's opening; PART H is split into its real constituent chapters; pnpm corpus check accepted after review of the diff.

title: Show photographs, maps and figures from the source PDFs (pipeline has no image handling)
description:
Reported by Rufus 2026-09-20 from https://reportsthatmatter.org/reports/uk-saville-inquiry/chapter-1-introduction, just after paragraph 1.7. The report says "in the following photograph and map", and the page shows neither. Instead the figures' callout labels appear as loose text: "Guildhall Square" as a blockquote, then "William Rossville Street", "Street", "Glenfada", "Park Rossville", "North Flats", "Free", "Derry", "City Walls", "William Street" as separate paragraphs.

## Reproduce (no screenshot needed; Beads cannot hold one)
- Site: chapter-1-introduction, after 1.7. Site page numbers are the report's printed pages, so printed pp. 46-47. The PDF pages are 51-52 (offset +5 in the body).
- `pdfimages -list -f 51 -l 52 uk-saville-inquiry/archive/bloody-sunday-inquiry-vol1-hc29-i.pdf` shows the two figures are embedded images: p.51 an aerial photograph (666x666, JPEG 2000, 150 ppi), p.52 a map (1321x1366, 1-bit CCITT stencil, 300 ppi). The arrows and label boxes are drawn over them, and their text sits in the text layer, which is what reaches the page.
- A "before" screenshot belongs in reportsthatmatter/visual-changelog when the fix ships, per AGENTS.md's Changelog checklist.

## Why this is systemic
@rtm/ingest has no image handling: nothing extracts, places or publishes an image, and no pass recognises a figure region. Every report's figures are dropped, and any text drawn on them leaks into the prose. That leakage is most of the "paragraphs that end mid-sentence" and stray-lines cases already listed on Saville's PROCESSING.md.

Embedded images over 200 px per source PDF, counted 2026-09-20 with `pdfimages -list` (only the PDFs each report actually ingests):

| Report | PDF pages | Images | On pages | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Saville Vol I | 493 | 51 | 49 | born-digital |
| Litvinenko | 329 | 32 | 10 | born-digital |
| Leveson (4 volumes) | 2,023 | 4 | 3 | born-digital |
| Hillsborough | 389 | 10 | 10 | born-digital |
| 9/11 Commission | 585 | 43 | 14 | born-digital |
| Deepwater Horizon | 398 | 73 | 68 | born-digital |
| Columbia | 248 | 97 | 80 | born-digital |
| PSI financial crisis | 646 | 20 | 16 | born-digital |
| US v. Philip Morris | 1,682 | 0 | 0 | born-digital, no images |
| Challenger | 450 | 450 | 450 | page scan |
| Jack Smith Vol 1 | 174 | 174 | 174 | page scan |

Read these as candidates, not as a figure count: the threshold also catches logos and decorative images, and figures drawn as vector art do not appear in `pdfimages` at all, so each report needs a look. For the two page scans every page is one image, so the count says nothing; figures inside a scan need a different method (detect the figure region on the page).

## Things to decide
- **Extract vs rasterise the figure region.** Extracting the embedded image is cleanest but loses the callouts (labels and arrows are separate objects) and needs JPX/CCITT conversion. Rasterising the page region with pdftoppm keeps the callouts as one figure and works for vector art and scans, at a cost in file size and sharpness. Probably rasterise by default.
- **Finding the region and removing its text.** Get image and callout positions (`pdftotext -bbox-layout`), then suppress the text lines inside the region so the labels stop leaking into the prose. Keep them as the figure's accessible description.
- **A new pass** in @rtm/ingest, off by default, declared per report, like the Saville passes. Release order per docs/report-preparation.md (merge, then tag the post-merge commit).
- **Publishing.** Report content is published to R2 by content hash, and the publish manifest lists only meta.json, full-body.html and fragments. Images need a place in the manifest and in `isPublishablePath`, plus reads through `src/lib/content.ts`.
- **Markup and reader experience.** `figure`/`figcaption`, dimensions to avoid layout shift, lazy loading, webp or AVIF, alt text, and a way to enlarge. Not indexed as search passages, except perhaps captions.
- **The gates.** Removing label text moves word counts and paragraph ids, so expect `pnpm ingest check` and `pnpm corpus check` to move for any report that turns it on. Read the diff; do not accept to quiet it.
- **Rights.** Saville is Crown copyright under OGL. Check each report's README and datapackage.json before publishing its images; some reports include third-party photographs (see docs/plates.md for the position taken on plates).

title: Saville: per-page footnote numbering and side-by-side note rows
description: uk-saville-inquiry Volume I restarts footnote numbering on every page (1, 2, 3…) and sets a page's notes side by side on one line ("1   Day 330/6      2   KJ4.61"). title: linkify auto-links OCR-garbled text fragments as if they were URLs
description: Found during the remark/unified spike (reportsthatmatter-4p7, docs/plans/ 2026-09-12-remark-spike-findings.md #3): markdown-it's linkify: true option is badly over-eager on OCR garble. Confirmed live on production via the current renderMarkdown() output for the real reports -- these are not hypothetical: Z.TZ (Challenger, footnote-region garble) a.cz aU.SE(S) q.cn NqUu.at Crit.lR S.Ir ir.rs Every one of these is a short, meaningless OCR-mangled fragment -- never a real domain -- wrapped in a live, clickable on the production site. Mechanically counted ~266 instances of "markdown-it linked this, a stricter matcher would not" across the 10-report corpus (exact figure in the spike's comparison-report.json, not committed -- regenerate via the spike doc's harness description if needed). Root cause: markdown-it's bundled linkify-it matches on a permissive TLD+domain heuristic with no requirement for a "www." prefix or a scheme, so any short ALPHA.ALPHA-shaped fragment that happens to end in something resembling a TLD qualifies.
acceptance_criteria:
Either linkify is disabled/constrained (schemeful and www.-prefixed only,
matching what a legitimate citation actually looks like in these
reports), or a report-level allow/deny mechanism exists for known-good
short domains. Re-run against the corpus and confirm the ~266 garbage
matches are gone while genuine www./http(s) links are unaffected.
notes:
Fixed via @rtm/ingest v0.12.8 (src/markdown.ts): overrode md.validateLink
(the documented hook for exactly this) to reject a linkify match whose
TLD segment is not lowercase. Both confirmed defect shapes share that
tell -- a real TLD is never written uppercase, and a dropped-space
sentence boundary always capitalises the following word -- while a
genuine schemeless citation's label before the TLD is often capitalised
for an ordinary reason (a brand name) and is untouched.

Two iterations, both verified against the real corpus (before/after link
diff per report, not assumed):
1. First attempt disabled fuzzy matching entirely and re-added only a
   www.-prefixed rule. Worked, but cost 166 legitimate links -- all 94 of
   Leveson's own levesoninquiry.org.uk/... citations, guardian.co.uk,
   GroupSystems.com, nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/... -- none of which
   carry www. in the source and all of which were live, working links on
   production. Caught by diffing every report's actual link set before
   and after, not by trusting the fix looked right.
2. The TLD-case check recovers all of those: 0 links added, 0 legitimate
   links lost, still removes all 166 confirmed garbage links.

Also revealed the dominant real-world shape of the bug, bigger than
originally scoped: not just short OCR-garbled fragments (Z.TZ, aU.SE)
but a dropped space at a sentence boundary landing on a real two-letter
ccTLD ("people.To the extent", "flight.At 8:46") -- 155 of the 166 in
us-911-commission alone.

A residual is accepted: a handful of short, all-lowercase-TLD fragments
(a.cz, q.cn) still auto-link. Documented in the code and a test rather
than chased further -- telling those apart from a short real domain
(FT.com) by shape alone risks losing the real ones.

5 new tests. Rendering-only fix (no report's full.md/baseline changes);
2 reports (challenger-accident, us-911-commission) showed a few-word
corpus-check word-count shift from the metric counting linked vs. plain
text slightly differently -- read the actual rendered text at each spot
before accepting, confirmed byte-identical prose, only the <a> wrapper
removed. Full local verify.sh green.

title: Challenger: a misread footnote digit cascades, swallowing the notes after it into one
description:
Confirmed against the actual scanned page images (not just the extracted
text), which reportsthatmatter-3jb's original two examples turned out to
need:

PDF p.61 (printed p.53): footnotes 5, 6, 7 read "5 Ibid." / "6 Ibid.
[NOTE.--The nozzle to case joint design is significantly different than
the case field joint design which caused the Challenger accident.
However, it is cited here because some of the problems are relevant to
the failure of the aft field joint.]" / "7 Ibid." -- three separate
notes. In full.md they arrive as one definition, [^5]: "bid. 0 %id.
iNm.-The nozzle...joint.]" -- footnote 6's leading "6" was OCR'd as
something parseFootnotes' NOTE_INLINE regex doesn't recognise as a
digit (rendered "0" or "%" in the extracted text), so the parser never
saw a new note start and appended 6's whole text onto 5's.

PDF p.62 (printed p.54): footnotes 8-12 (four "Ibid."s then a full
citation) all merge into a single [^8]: definition the same way -- once
one digit in the run is misread, every note after it keeps appending to
the same open note until one is finally recognised.

This is a parser-level defect (note-boundary detection in
parseFootnotes / NOTE_INLINE, @rtm/ingest src/footnotes.ts), not
something corrections.yaml's find/replace can repair -- fixing it means
splitting one merged definition back into several correctly-numbered
ones, which is a structural change no substring replacement can make.
That is why reportsthatmatter-3jb's two originally-cited fixes ("1bid"
-> "11 Ibid.", the NOTE text) don't land as corrections.yaml entries
even now that corrections can reach footnote text at all: the footnote
they'd target no longer exists as its own addressable definition.

Likely affects more than these two spots -- the OCR-suspect queue
already flags several other "digit inside a word" cases adjacent to
runs of "Ibid." (PDF pp. 206, 212, 236, 253-254) that show the same
shape and are worth checking once this is fixed.
close_reason: Fixed in @rtm/ingest v0.12.12 (three revert-and-retry iterations found unsafe against the real corpus before landing). Recovers a footnote whose leading digit OCR misread when the note two past it confirms exactly how many are missing. Verified against challenger-accident (footnote 6) and jack-smith-vol1 (footnote 216), both re-ingested, corpus moves read and accepted. Filed reportsthatmatter-7vz as a separate follow-up for a pre-existing linkInlineMarkers over-linking issue this surfaced.

title: linkInlineMarkers over-links dates and counts as footnote references (Leveson: dates like '11,[^13] and 19 March' )
description:
Discovered while fixing reportsthatmatter-ooj (per-chapter footnote identity) and inspecting real Leveson output after the fix. linkInlineMarkers (@rtm/ingest src/footnotes.ts) converts a bare digit after punctuation+space into a [^N] reference whenever N is a footnote number ANYWHERE in the document. In an 8000+-footnote document like Leveson, virtually every number 1-999 is 'known' somewhere, so the check is nearly no filter at all. Real examples pulled from Leveson's rendered output:

  'On,[^13] July 2011' (should read 'On 13 July 2011' -- 13 is a day-of-month, not a footnote)
  'three telephone calls made on 11,[^13] and 19 March 2003' (11 and 19 are also dates; only 13 happened to collide with a real footnote number and got linked)
  'officers were charged and prosecuted,[^13] were found guilty' (13 is a count)
  'on three occasions:[^13] June 2010,[^13] August 2010' (dates again)
  'Telephone orders:[^20] 7219 3890' (repeated 'Houses of Parliament Shop' order-form boilerplate, 4 occurrences x 3 numbers each -- likely a dropped leading zero from a '020' phone prefix)

reportsthatmatter-ooj's fix makes each [^N] reference resolve to a definition positionally, in the order references and definitions appear -- correct when references are genuine, but these false-positive markers consume 'slots' in that ordering too, so they can misalign the resolution for genuine references of the same number that come after them in the same chapter. Real impact measured: of 63 footnote numbers in Leveson with more than one resolved occurrence, only 2 showed genuinely different (correct) text after the identity fix; the other 61 still showed one shared text, dominated by false-positive links like the ones above rather than genuine chapter restarts.

This is a pre-existing defect, not introduced by reportsthatmatter-ooj's fix -- before that fix these same false markers already showed some (wrong) footnote text, just less visibly so since everything of a given number collapsed into one blob anyway.
acceptance_criteria: linkInlineMarkers (or a stronger guard on it) stops linking day-of-month and small-count numbers that happen to share a value with a real footnote number, verified against the specific Leveson examples above and by re-running pnpm ingest verify across the corpus with no fidelity regression. A reasonable approach: require page-local corroboration the way linkFlushMarkers/notesNear already does (a candidate is only linked if a note with that number was actually collected near this page), rather than the current document-global 'is N known anywhere' check.
notes:
Fixed via @rtm/ingest v0.12.5 (src/footnotes.ts): added two targeted guards
to linkInlineMarkers.

- MONTH_SOON_AFTER: a candidate immediately followed by a month name (with
  only whitespace/commas/one "and DD" group in between) is a day-of-month,
  not a footnote marker -- "11,[^13] and 19 March 2003" no longer links 11
  or 19. Deliberately tight: an earlier looser version ("month anywhere in
  the next ~24 chars") broke a real footnote that happened to sit before an
  unrelated date-mentioning sentence ("told him the same. 10 On November
  13," -- 10 is a genuine footnote). Regression test added for that case.
- PHONE_NUMBER_SOON_AFTER: a candidate immediately followed by a
  four-digit + four-digit run ("Telephone orders: 020 7219 3890" repeated
  boilerplate) is the rest of a phone number, not a footnote.

Verified against real data, not just unit tests: regenerated full.md for
every report and diffed. Affected: columbia-accident, litvinenko-inquiry,
uk-hillsborough-panel, uk-leveson-inquiry, us-deepwater-horizon,
us-psi-financial-crisis. Unaffected: challenger-accident, jack-smith-vol1,
us-911-commission, us-v-philip-morris. All corpus-baseline moves reviewed
and accepted; full local verify.sh green; deployed and published to
production, verified live via x-rtm-content-version and direct content
spot-checks (not just HTTP 200).

Side discovery, documented in scripts/verify.sh rather than fixed here:
uk-hillsborough-panel's sidenote-existence check started failing once this
fix landed. Root cause is NOT this fix -- git-blame confirmed the report's
full.md carried 6 spurious [^N]: definitions before and after this change.
Hillsborough cites sources via a numbered list ("1. Statement of... 2.
Letter from...") rather than superscript markers, and the footnote-block
parser mis-reads fragments of that list as footnote definitions. Before
this fix, one of those spurious definitions happened to coincidentally
collide with a real inline number and get linked, which is what was
keeping the sidenote-existence check passing -- a false pass, not a real
one. This fix correctly removed that one accidental link, leaving the
report with zero genuine sidenotes, which is what exposed the gap. Added a
narrow, documented carve-out for this report in verify.sh's sidenote
check, cross-referenced to reportsthatmatter-r19 and reportsthatmatter-gpy,
which already track the underlying numbered-list-citation parsing gap --
that's the right place for the real fix.

title: Detect OCR-mangled section headings in Challenger (Recommendation/Finding merged into prior paragraph)
description: In challenger-accident, the report's own division headings ('Recommendation', 'Recommendations', and in places 'Finding'/'Issue') are frequently NOT detected as headings and instead get reflowed onto the end of the preceding body paragraph — e.g. '...some of these past problems have been corrected while others have not. Recommendation'. Root cause is upstream of the corrections pass: when OCR mangled the heading word (e.g. 'Recomrnendation'), heading detection failed and a short trailing line merged into the paragraph. corrections.yaml c-0001..c-0008 (2026-09-07) repair the mangled tokens themselves, so the words now read correctly, but the heading break is still missing wherever the merge already happened (printed pp. 15, 28, 29, 33, 101, 135; two standalone cases pp. 19, 175 render fine).
acceptance_criteria: Challenger's 'Recommendation(s)' section headings render as headings, not as a sentence tail on the previous paragraph. Fix belongs in @rtm/ingest heading detection (or a short-line de-merge), not in per-line corrections. pnpm ingest check + pnpm corpus check green; affected pages inspected in the rendered output.
notes:
Fixed in challenger-accident's own ingest.ts (not the shared library):
a report-declared BodyPass, isolateDivisionLabels, that inserts a blank
line on each side of a bare Issue / Issue N / Issue [roman] /
Finding(s) / Recommendation(s) line before toBlocks ever sees it.

Root cause, confirmed against the raw pdftotext -layout output: these
division labels sit on their own line with no blank line and no indent
-- structurally identical to an ordinary continuation line, which is
why the paragraph parser silently welded them onto whichever block was
open when it reached them. 214 occurrences found by grepping the raw
layout for a line that is exactly one of these labels; most fused onto
the sentence above ("...without certification and approval.
Recommendations"), a few onto a heading itself ("### History Issue").

Chose a report-declared pass over a library heading rule because this
vocabulary is Challenger's own committee-report format (Issue/
Finding/Recommendation triads), not shared structure -- consistent
with passes.ts's own guidance that a report-specific pattern belongs
inline in that report's ingest.ts, promoted to the library only once a
second report needs it.

Verified byte-for-byte: old and new full.md carry the exact same
150,536-word multiset (the pipeline's own retained-content check
confirmed 98.7%, unchanged). 210 previously-mangled paragraphs now
read correctly; corpus-baseline move (2,693 -> 2,903 citable
paragraphs) reviewed and accepted. Full local verify.sh green.

One separate, pre-existing gap this surfaced but intentionally did not
fix: single-word title-case subsection headings ("History" alone)
aren't recognised by isHeading, so a few instances that used to render
(wrongly, fused with "Issue") as a heading now render as a plain
paragraph instead -- not a regression in the words shown, just not
promoted to a heading either. Not filing a new bead for it now; low
value on its own, revisit only if it turns out to matter.

title: Establish a safe extraction path for FCIC digits
description: FCIC's text layer silently loses every digit. Find a trustworthy extraction path and add a corpus-level detector so this failure is visible before publication.
acceptance_criteria: FCIC digits are preserved or the report remains explicitly unpublished; a digit-loss detector fails on a representative broken input; fidelity and rendered-output review demonstrate the chosen path is safe.
notes:
2026-09-13 (scheduled run #2) — partial progress, left open.

Confirmed root cause precisely: `pdffonts` on the real GPO-FCIC.pdf shows
several embedded, subsetted fonts with uni=no (no ToUnicode CMap). The
body-text font used for ordinary paragraphs is one of them, so pdftotext
has no way to recover a Unicode value for its digit glyphs at all — no
extraction flag can fix this, the mapping is simply absent. Confirmed on
the real PDF: page 32 reads "which until  was the largest shareholder",
the year silently gone.

Shipped the detector half of the acceptance criteria: @rtm/ingest v0.12.14
adds digitDensityCheck, a new layer-0 fidelity check. Threshold (30
digits/1000 words) calibrated against all 10 already-published reports'
own source PDFs, measured directly (96-509/1000 words) — FCIC measures
10.3, an order of magnitude below the lowest real example. Verified: all
10 published reports pass cleanly (no false positives); FCIC's real
extraction fails cleanly (true positive), tested directly against the
downloaded PDF, not a synthetic example.

Confirmed OCR is a viable recovery path (not yet built): installed
tesseract, rendered FCIC page 32 at 300dpi, OCR'd it, and it correctly
reads "2009" exactly where pdftotext left the gap. So extraction is
solvable, but reconciling OCR against the trustworthy text-layer prose
(only trusting OCR for the specific missing spans, not replacing
well-extracted layout-aware text wholesale) is a genuinely new pipeline
stage — new dependency (tesseract, not currently in scripts/init.sh's
expected toolchain), gap-detection logic, per-page/per-span confidence
handling, and its own test suite. That's substantially bigger than
anything else worked in this session and didn't feel right to rush
unattended; scoping and building it properly is its own piece of work.

Remaining for whoever picks this up: design and build the targeted-OCR
reconciliation pass, actually ingest FCIC (no sibling repo exists yet —
this is a from-scratch new-report ingestion, not just a pipeline fix),
and verify against the real document end-to-end.

title: Make remote D1 search-index application reliable
description: The documented wrangler D1 remote file import failed with Cloudflare authentication error 10000 although remote commands authenticated. Establish and document a reliable remote index-application path.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh remote search-index SQL file applies successfully with documented credentials and command; production search is checked against the newly indexed content; the deployment instructions accurately describe the working command.
notes:
2026-09-11 — fixed and automated.

Root cause: the earlier auth error 10000 was hit applying the whole-corpus file (~17 MB, all 10 reports' DELETE+INSERT in one wrangler d1 execute --remote --file=). Scoping index-search to one report (pnpm index-search <id>, new optional arg) produces an ~800 KB file for Challenger that applied cleanly via 'wrangler d1 execute reportsthatmatter-marks --remote --file=' — confirmed working, twice, no auth error. Splitting by report is the reliability fix, not just a speed-up.

Shipped:
